title: AAFP and ISFM Feline Environmental Needs Guidelines
excerpt: The guidelines emphasize that cats need adequate vertical space including shelves, perches, and climbing structures. Vertical territory is essential for cats to feel secure and exercise natural behaviors. The guidelines recommend multiple elevated resting places at various heights throughout the home environment, allowing cats to choose their preferred vantage points. While specific heights are not mandated, the emphasis is on providing options at different levels to accommodate individual preferences and physical abilities.
authors: Ellis, S. L., Rodan, I., Carney, H. C., et al.
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

title: Feline Environmental Needs - Cat Friendly Homes (AAFP)
excerpt: Cats benefit from vertical territory that allows them to climb, perch, and observe their environment from elevated positions. Wall-mounted shelves, cat trees, and window perches provide essential vertical space. The guidelines note that elevated spaces give cats a sense of security and control over their environment. Multiple levels allow cats to escape from stressors and choose their preferred resting locations.

title: Catification: Creating a Cat-Friendly Home
excerpt: Jackson Galaxy's catification principles emphasize creating vertical pathways and elevated spaces for cats. Wall shelves and 'cat superhighways' should be positioned at heights that allow cats to navigate without touching the ground. The recommended height for primary walking shelves is typically 60-90cm (24-36 inches) from the floor, which corresponds to a comfortable jumping and walking height for most adult cats. This height allows cats to move confidently while still being able to jump down safely. Narrow shelves (15-20cm wide) are sufficient for cats to walk along walls.
author: Jackson Galaxy
note: Popular cat behaviorist and author of 'Catification: Designing a Happy and Stylish Home for Your Cat and You'
